summary: An excerpt from a fiction novel (Book 4, part 112) in which Leeza visits a wizard who lives in a clean, tidy home served by robots. He feeds her, outfits her with new clothes including a bra printed by his machine, and sends her home with a light and a cover story. The excerpt then shifts to Valentine and her mother in a food-scarce, post-siege setting, where Valentine has stopped carrying water after her father's death.
one_line: Leeza receives food, clothes, and a cover story from a wizard with robot servants, while Valentine and her mother face siege-era food shortages.
key_facts: The wizard's home has robots that do the dishes, tidy up, and wipe up slushy footprints.
Laser-lights measure Leeza when she arrives, like the measuring lasers once used at clothing stores.
By the end of dinner, the robots have produced two pairs of fresh trousers, two wooly jumpers, a heavy winter coat, and three pairs of white cotton pants.
Leeza's old pants had gone grey because she had to launder them rather than get them printed fresh on Sundays.
Leeza says, "My mother taught me to kill," while holding the knife she used on the hamburger.
The wizard explains that if the printer thinks you need a bra, it makes a bra.
The wizard's bathroom has six toothbrushes beside the sink in a holder.
The wizard tells Leeza, "I have a lot of friends who come and see me now and again."
When Leeza asks why his place seems untouched by the war, he answers, "I'm the wizard, that's why."
The wizard gives Leeza a warm slicker with a hood and one of his little pea-lights to carry.
The wizard tells Leeza to say she met a wizard if her mother asks where she has been, but Leeza decides she will say she met someone from the city.
The wizard calls Leeza "a clever girl."
One week after her father died, Valentine stopped carrying water.
Valentine's mother says there is not enough food and that breakfast is only dried fruit because the cereal is gone.
Valentine's mother suggests that if Valentine digs in the trenches, they will get 150 grams of bread.
